page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. It includes 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1 data cache per core. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware benchmark testing indicates exceptional single-threaded execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2877 and a stress-ng single-core result of 3783.48 placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Multi-core execution is similarly robust, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 21577 and a PassMark CPU score of 56708.47. Uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth reaches 103.4 GB/sec for read operations and 68.56 GB/sec for write operations. Data processing tasks show strong results, including single-threaded gzip compression at 41.24 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 247.64 GB/sec.

The E32as_v7 includes no local storage and bundles no GPUs, requiring reliance on remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent file and root system disks. While prompt processing and text generation for small language models (135M) deliver high throughput at over 400 tokens/sec, large models such as 70B parameter architectures demonstrate poor text generation performance at 2.37 tokens/sec due to the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators.

This server type offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments that demand fast per-core compute without the overhead of attached physical NVMe drives. Recommended workloads include in-memory caching layers such as Redis, medium-to-large relational databases, compilation suites, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure E32as_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, running on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. Benchmarks show upper-tier single-thread performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2877 and multi-core score of 21577, complemented by uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 103 GB/sec. The instance features zero local storage, requiring network-attached Azure Premium Storage, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. CPU-based execution remains strong for compression and moderate AI prompt processing, but large-parameter model inference is constrained by hardware limits. Given its 8 GB per core memory profile and high CPU clock, the E32as_v7 is tailored for in-memory databases, large caching layers, continuous integration pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise software.
